newsitem.title: UK: Granada sells London Hyde Park Hotel to Mandarin.
newsitem.headline: Granada sells London Hyde Park Hotel to Mandarin.

text.p: British media and leisure company Granada Group Plc on Tuesday sold London's Hyde Park Hotel for 86 million pounds ($144 million) as it kicked off a planned series of luxury property disposals.

The 185-room site in the heart of London was bought by a subsidiary of Mandarin Oriental International, the luxury hotel arm of Bermuda-based conglomerate Jardine Matheson Holdings which operates in the far East.
It was the first move in the planned disposal of 17 luxury hotels Granada acquired as part of its 3.9 billion pound takeover of the family-run Forte empire last January.

Granada said it hopes to complete the disposals by early 1997. Other properties on the market include the George V in Paris and New York's Westbury and Plaza Athenee. The sales are expected to raise a total of some 800-900 million pounds.
Granada, which has extensive interests in British commercial television, will publish full-year results on Wednesday. Pre-tax profits are forecast to top 450 million pounds. ($1=.5970 Pound)
